description: Review results for the cross-study consistency queue (soa2usdm.consistency), kept by hand. One entry per reviewed subject: a queue phrase, a within-study entry or a flag. outcomes_seen records the outcomes at review time; the queue page marks an entry whose outcomes have changed since, and lists reviewed subjects that have left the queue. The queue itself decides nothing; these entries record a reviewer's reading and where the work goes.

reviews.note: Rule as designed: VS-OV settles VS for a measurement only inside a vital-signs panel (documents/activity-routing.md). 'Height and weight' panels are not vital-signs panels, so those members stay open, like the standalone rows.
Same pattern as weight: members routed VS by the vital-signs panel rule RT-11; the standalone row (NCT04004988) has a weak hit, TEMP in VS and in BS/DO, and the input does not say whose temperature.

Mechanism, not AI: the grain label path drops the short-code hit ('short code only, not taken: HIV (MB)'), the member path keeps it as a weak hit and routes. Same phrase, same lookup, two treatments. With the CT / VAS short-code hits.
As hiv: short-code hit TSH (LB) dropped on the grain label path, kept as a weak hit on the member path.

NCT01797120: the footnote 'Patients on antiviral prophylaxis treatment or positive HBV antibodies should be tested for HBV-DNA ...' fires RT-1 (IS) on the annotation only; the row becomes weak and the HBDNA (MB) test-identity hit is set aside. The footnote says who is tested, not what is measured. Question for the rules: how an annotation-only rule match ranks against a label test-identity hit.
The protocols differ: NCT03548935 context lists four analytes (panel); NCT03693430 lists one, hsCRP (named test, no test code on the label).
The protocols differ: NCT03637764 names two analytes, isatuximab and atezolizumab (panel); NCT04557384 one, ramucirumab (named test, PC by RT-9).
The standalone row of the hbv dna queue entry: weak because of the annotation-only RT-1 match; the member HBV-DNA in the same study routes MB.
The only member from protocol context is the panel label itself, 'Urine drug screen (including cotinine)', routed LB via DRUGSCR (peeled hit). A panel that is its own member.
Stays open. Named test gives PC; panel (rosuvastatin and pirtobrutinib in the same samples) would give 'panel, not split' and lose the PC route. The label names only rosuvastatin.

Other vs panel does not change routing: a panel would have no named-test members. 2026-11-08 (step 4 A): re-decided after the grain rules 1.3.0 release (prompt 1.6.0) as unsure, footnote xannot-027 lists survival, subsequent therapies and new malignancy; outcome unchanged (no own row).
Grain other in all six studies; a logistics step.
